assertions.description: audioContext.audioWorklet.port is a MessagePort and the same object on every read.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = new AudioContext(); const p = c.audioWorklet.port; const ok = p instanceof MessagePort && p === c.audioWorklet.port; c.close(); return ok; })()

assertions.description: port is readonly: assigning to audioWorklet.port does not replace the MessagePort.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = new AudioContext(); const before = c.audioWorklet.port; try { c.audioWorklet.port = null; } catch (e) {} const ok = !!before && c.audioWorklet.port === before; c.close(); return ok; })()

assertions.description: After addModule(), a message posted on audioWorklet.port is received by top-level code in AudioWorkletGlobalScope via its own port and answered, with no AudioWorkletNode created.
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new AudioContext(); try { await c.audioWorklet.addModule('/v160/shared-messageport-for-audioworklet/port-handshake/handshake-module.js'); const p = c.audioWorklet.port; if (!p) return false; const r = await new Promise((res) => { const t = setTimeout(() => res(null), 2000); p.onmessage = (e) => { clearTimeout(t); res(e.data); }; p.postMessage({ type: 'ping', t: 1 }); }); return !!r && r.type === 'pong' && r.typeofPort === 'object'; } finally { c.close(); } })()

assertions.description: audioWorklet.port.postMessage accepts a transfer list: a transferred ArrayBuffer is detached on the main thread.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = new AudioContext(); try { const b = new ArrayBuffer(16); c.audioWorklet.port.postMessage(b, [b]); return b.byteLength === 0; } finally { c.close(); } })()

assertions.description: AudioWorkletNode.prototype still exposes its own per-processor port; the shared port is added alongside it, not instead of it.
